title: Appendix A — Data collation
text:
A.1 Key metadata
In this section, we write various cell metadata to a csv for public sharing of the data.
We read in key metadata from various files, store it in one data frame, and write it to a csv.
Show the code
# if there's no seurat object, read it in
if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$seurat_file_postCellTyping)
}

#cell ID, major cell type, minor cell type, x/y positions from Seurat file
meta = seu.obj@meta.data[,c("cell_ID", "x_slide_mm", "y_slide_mm", "major_cell_type", "minor_cell_type")]

# Novae domain
novae_9 <- readRDS(paste0(niche_dir, "/Data/novae_domains_9_namedAssignments.rds"))
meta$novaeDomain <- novae_9[rownames(meta)]

# Tumor lobe designation
meta$tumorLobe <- NA
meta[results_list$upper_lobe_cells, "tumorLobe"] <- "Interdigitated"
meta[results_list$lower_lobe_cells, "tumorLobe"] <- "Dense"

# Smoothed pathway scores in tumor cells
key_pathways = c("JAK-STAT" = "REACTOME_GENE_AND_PROTEIN_EXPRESSION_BY_JAK_STAT_SIGNALING_AFTER_INTERLEUKIN_12_STIMULATION",
                 "MHC-1" = "REACTOME_ANTIGEN_PRESENTATION_FOLDING_ASSEMBLY_AND_PEPTIDE_LOADING_OF_CLASS_I_MHC",
                 "NF-kappa B" = "REACTOME_REGULATION_OF_NF_KAPPA_B_SIGNALING",
                 "TNF" = "REACTOME_TNF_SIGNALING"
)

idx = which(meta$major_cell_type == "Tumor")
  
# Gather score for each pathway
for(i in 1:4){
  pathway = key_pathways[i]
  
  # Read in smoothed pathway scores
  smoothed_path_score <- readRDS(file = paste0(immNeigh_dir, "/Data/xy_smoothed_tumor_", pathway, ".rds"))
  meta[,paste0(gsub("-", "_", names(key_pathways[i])), "SmoothScore_Tumor")] <- NA
  meta[idx,paste0(gsub("-", "_", names(key_pathways[i])), "SmoothScore_Tumor")] <- smoothed_path_score[1,rownames(meta[idx,])]
}

# Distance to vasculature
dist2vessel <-readRDS(file = paste0(vessel_dir, "/Data/dist2vessel.rds"))
meta$VesselDistance <- dist2vessel[,1]

# Neighborhood glycolysis score
smoothed_glyc <- readRDS(file = paste0(metabolism_dir, "/Data/xy_smoothed_glycolysis.rds"))
meta$neighborhoodGlycolysis <- smoothed_glyc[1,rownames(meta)]

# Cell cycle prediction
cellcycle <- readRDS(paste0(prolif_dir, "/Data/cell_cycle_predictions.rds"))
meta$cellCyclePrediction <- cellcycle[rownames(meta)]

# Patch assignment for proliferation DE
meta$PatchAssignment <- NA
patches <- readRDS(paste0(prolif_dir, "/Data/patchDE.RDS"))
meta[names(patches), "PatchAssignment"] <- patches


write.csv(meta, file = paste0(objects_dir, "/derivedMetadata.csv"))

In this first chapter, we complete preprocessing steps on the breast cancer dataset. We begin with a Seurat object exported from AtoMx® SIP before any processing. We perform quality control to remove low quality cells and then proceed through normalization, dimension reduction, and cell typing.
In this section we run standard QC steps on the breast cancer dataset.

1.1.2 Per FOV QC

FOVQC
Use the CosMx-specific algorithm FOVQC to check for any FOVs that show loss of signal.


Show the code
# Object and color setup

if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$raw_seurat_file)
}

## Run FOV QC
if (!file.exists(paste0(qc_dir, "/Data/fovqc.RDS"))) {
   source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Nanostring-Biostats/CosMx-Analysis-Scratch-Space/Main/_code/FOV%20QC/FOV%20QC%20utils.R")  
  allbarcodes <- readRDS(url("https://github.com/Nanostring-Biostats/CosMx-Analysis-Scratch-Space/raw/Main/_code/FOV%20QC/barcodes_by_panel.RDS"))
  barcodes <- allbarcodes[["Hs_WTX"]]
  
  smallfovs <- names(which(table(seu.obj@meta.data$fov) < 500))
  tempuse <- !is.element(seu.obj@meta.data$fov, smallfovs)
  
  sharedgenes <- intersect(barcodemap[,1], rownames(seu.obj@assays$RNA@counts))
  res <- runFOVQC(counts = t(seu.obj@assays$RNA@counts)[tempuse, sharedgenes], 
                  xy = seu.obj@meta.data[,c("x_slide_mm", "y_slide_mm")][tempuse, ], 
                  fov = as.character(seu.obj@meta.data$fov[tempuse]), 
                  barcodemap = barcodemap[match(sharedgenes, barcodemap[, 1]), ],
                  max_prop_loss = 0.5, max_totalcounts_loss = 0.5)  
  str(res)
  saveRDS(res, file = paste0(qc_dir, "/Data/fovqc.RDS"))
} else {
  res <- readRDS(paste0(qc_dir, "/Data/fovqc.RDS"))
}

# Plot FOV QC results following FOV QC vignette from Scratch Space.

# Show flagged FOVs in space
png(filename = paste0(qc_dir, "/Plots/flagged_FOVs_in_space.png"), 
    width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", res = 300)
mapFlaggedFOVs(res)
dev.off()

# Plot loss in total signal strength:
png(filename = paste0(qc_dir, "/Plots/overall_signal_loss_in_space.png"), 
    width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", res = 300)
FOVSignalLossSpatialPlot(res, shownames = TRUE)
dev.off()

Show the code
knitr::include_graphics(paste0(qc_dir, "/Plots/flagged_FOVs_in_space.png"))









There is one FOV that gets flagged due to low counts. As this is on the edge of the tissue, this is not too surprising and we will keep this FOV in our analysis.
Loss in total signal strength:


Show the code
knitr::include_graphics(paste0(qc_dir, "/Plots/overall_signal_loss_in_space.png"))









The changes in total signal strength tend to follow biology and do not track with individual FOVs. Thus, we will not exclude any FOVs for further analysis based on these results.



1.1.3 Cell Flagging
Flag cells that failed any of the QC above and plot these in space. We’re looking for areas with high failure rates, suggesting technical artifacts (local tissue peeling, blurriness, etc).


Show the code
# Object and color setup

if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$raw_seurat_file)
}

# Flag cells that failed tx or area QC
seu.obj@meta.data <- seu.obj@meta.data %>%
  mutate(qcCellsFlagged = case_when(
    Area.um2 > area_cutoff ~ "TRUE",
    nCount_RNA < lower_tx_cutoff ~ "TRUE",
    nCount_RNA > upper_tx_cutoff ~ "TRUE",
    TRUE ~ "FALSE"
  ))

# Plotting XY
ggplot(seu.obj@meta.data, 
       aes(x = x_slide_mm, y = y_slide_mm, color = qcCellsFlagged)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.001) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "lightgrey", "TRUE" = "red")) +
  theme_classic() +
  coord_fixed() 
ggsave(filename = paste0(qc_dir, "/Plots/XY_QCflaggedCells.png"),
       width = 16, height = 16, units = "in")

# Remove cells failing QC and save seurat object
seu.obj <- seu.obj[,which(seu.obj@meta.data$qcCellsFlagged == "FALSE")]
saveRDS(seu.obj, file = paste0(objects_dir, "/seurat_object_postQC.rds"))
results_list$seurat_file_postQC = paste0(objects_dir, "/seurat_object_postQC.rds")
  saveRDS(results_list, results_list_file)


Flagged cells in XY space:


Show the code
knitr::include_graphics(paste0(qc_dir, "/Plots/XY_QCflaggedCells.png"))









From this plot, it’s clear that the flagged cells aren’t evenly spread across the tissue - there are round-ish structures that are getting flagged at a much higher rate, suggesting that there’s a structure in the tissue that has lower counts for some reason. Given this, we have used a liberal cutoff of 200 counts per cell. From a bit of exploration, it’s clear that these cells are primarily getting flagged due to having low counts. Returning to the immunofluorescence images, these likely mark regions of necrosis.

title: 1  Data Preprocessing
text:
1.4 Cell Typing
In this section we assign major and minor cell types using a combination of iterative unsupervised clustering and marker-based hierarchical assignment.


Click to show/hide cell typing steps

This section performs cell typing of the dataset with a multistep approach. First, we use unsupervised clustering to broadly group the cells. For some of these major cell types (tumor cells, fibroblasts, vascular cells) we subset and perform unsupervised clustering a second time on the subset. For immune cells, we use the marker-based hierarchical cell typing approach HieraType.

1.4.1 Unsupervised clustering
Cluster cells with Seurat function.


Show the code
if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$seurat_file_postUMAP)
}

# With Seurat
seu.obj <- Seurat::FindClusters(seu.obj, graph.name = "umapgrph", resolution = 0.7)

# Plot it in XY space with random colors
set.seed(2024)
my_pal <- sample(colors(distinct = TRUE), length(unique(seu.obj@meta.data$seurat_clusters)))
names(my_pal) <- as.character(unique(seu.obj@meta.data$seurat_clusters))
ggplot(seu.obj@meta.data,
        aes(x = x_slide_mm, y = y_slide_mm, 
            color = as.factor(seurat_clusters))) +  
    geom_point(size = 0.1) +  
  scale_color_manual(values = my_pal) +
    theme_classic() +  
    coord_fixed() +  
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size=10)))
ggsave(filename = paste0(dimRed_dir, "/Plots/XY_leiden.png"),
       width = 8, height = 16, units = "in")

# Plot each cell type separately
for (ct in unique(seu.obj@meta.data$seurat_clusters)){
  ggplot(seu.obj@meta.data[order(seu.obj@meta.data$seurat_clusters == ct),],
         aes(x = x_slide_mm, y = y_slide_mm, 
             color = seurat_clusters==ct)) +  
    geom_point(size = 0.05) +  
    scale_color_manual(values = c("lightgrey", "red"), name = ct) +
    theme_classic() +  
    coord_fixed() +  
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size=10)))
  ggsave(filename = paste0(dimRed_dir, "/Plots/XY_leiden_", ct, ".png"),
         width = 8, height = 16, units = "in")
}


# Plot it in UMAP space
DimPlot(seu.obj, group.by = "seurat_clusters", reduction = "umap", label = T) +
  scale_color_manual(values = my_pal)
ggsave(filename = paste0(dimRed_dir, "/Plots/umap_leiden.png"))

# Plot each cell type separately in UMAP space
plot.df <- seu.obj@meta.data
plot.df$UMAP1 <- seu.obj@reductions$umap@cell.embeddings[,1]
plot.df$UMAP2 <- seu.obj@reductions$umap@cell.embeddings[,2]

for (ct in unique(plot.df$seurat_clusters)){
  ggplot(plot.df[order(plot.df$seurat_clusters == ct),],
         aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, 
             color = seurat_clusters==ct)) +  
    geom_point(size = 0.05, alpha = 0.5) +  
    scale_color_manual(values = c("lightgrey", "red"), name = ct) +
    theme_classic() +  
    coord_fixed() +  
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size=10)))
  ggsave(filename = paste0(dimRed_dir, "/Plots/UMAP_leiden_", ct, ".png"),
         width = 10, height = 8, units = "in")
}

# Generate a marker heatmap with HieraType functions
## prepare data for marker gene heatmap:
fc_subclus_ctl_gran <- clusterwise_foldchange_metrics(seu.obj[["RNA"]]@counts
                                                      ,metadata = seu.obj@meta.data
                                                      ,cluster_column = "seurat_clusters"
)
# subtract background from the mean per-cluster expression profiles:
neg_counts <- seu.obj@assays$negprobes$counts
for (name in unique(seu.obj@meta.data$seurat_clusters)) {
  isthiscelltype <- seu.obj@meta.data$seurat_clusters == name
  meannegthiscelltype <- Matrix::mean(neg_counts[, isthiscelltype])
  
  fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster_expr[fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster == name] <- 
    pmax(fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster_expr[fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster == name] - meannegthiscelltype, 0)
}
# create the heatmap:
hm_semiSup <- add_ncells(marker_heatmap(fc_subclus_ctl_gran))

png(filename = paste0(dimRed_dir, "/Plots/heatmap_leiden_negRemoved.png"),
    width = 24, height = 8, units = "in", res = 300)
print(hm_semiSup)
dev.off()

# Save seurat object
results_list$leiden_color_pal <- my_pal
results_list$seurat_file_postLeiden <- paste0(objects_dir, "/seurat_object_postLeiden.rds")
saveRDS(results_list, results_list_file)
saveRDS(seu.obj, results_list$seurat_file_postLeiden)

1.4.2 Refine cell type annotations
These unsupervised clusters do a pretty good job of splitting apart major cell types. We follow this up by naming and refining this initial clustering result based on spatial distribution, top marker genes, and position in UMAP space. In particular, we’ll recluster the tumor cells on their own to reduce the number of clusters and subcluster the fibroblast and vascular clusters. Additionally, we’ll use HieraType to perform targeted marker-based annotation of the immune cells. We start with our evaluation and planned actions for each cluster:

We start with fibroblasts since this cluster is near immune clusters and may be partially overlapping. The initial unsupervised clustering had only one fibroblast cluster, but from previous experience with this sample we expect that we should be able to identify a few subtypes. Additionally, it appears that the cluster that is mostly fibroblast may also contain some immune cells. Here we take the fibroblast cells, repeat initial preprocessing so that highly variable genes are chosen based on these cells, and use unsupervised clustering to separate these cells into multiple clusters, some of which we’ll add to the immune cells for HieraType clustering.


Show the code
if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$seurat_file_postLeiden)
}

# Subset the seurat object to only include fibroblast cluster
fibro_leiden <- c(2)
fibro_idx <- which(seu.obj@meta.data$seurat_clusters %in% fibro_leiden)
seu.fibro <- seu.obj[,fibro_idx]

# Repeat preprocessing, dimension reduction, and leiden clustering
seu.fibro <- NormalizeData(seu.fibro, 
                         normalization.method = "RC", 
                         scale.factor = mean(seu.fibro@meta.data$nCount_RNA))
seu.fibro <- FindVariableFeatures(seu.fibro, 
                                selection.method = "vst", 
                                nfeatures = 3000)
seu.fibro <- ScaleData(seu.fibro)
seu.fibro <- RunPCA(seu.fibro, 
                  features = VariableFeatures(seu.fibro))
umapobj <- make_umap(seu.fibro@reductions$pca@cell.embeddings)

seu.fibro[["umap"]] <- umapobj$ump

title: 2  Pathways - AUCell
text:
In this section we use AUCell to calculate pathway activity across thousands of pathways. We use pathways found in the Reactome database for this analysis.
AUCell operates independently on cells and on pathways, so we use chunking of our dataset to run all these calculations.


Show the code
# Read in gene sets and chunk for processing
# original location: gene.sets <- readRDS("~/data/dan/imputation_smoothing/breast_reanalysis/gene.sets.list.rds")[["human"]]
gene.sets <- readRDS(paste0(pathway_dir, "/Data/gene.sets.list.rds"))[["human"]]
chunks <- data.table(strt=unique(c(seq(1, length(gene.sets), 100), length(gene.sets))))
chunks[,stp:=data.table::shift(strt, 1, type="lead")]
chunks <- chunks[-c(.N)]
chunks[1:(.N-1),stp:=stp-1]

# if there's no seurat object, read it in
if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$seurat_file_postCellTyping)
}

# Extract normalized data and meta data
tc <- Matrix::colSums(seu.obj[["RNA"]]@counts)
scale.factor <- mean(tc)
normed <- seu.obj[["RNA"]]@counts %*% Matrix::Diagonal(x = scale.factor / tc, names = TRUE)
met <- data.table(seu.obj@meta.data)

# Calculate median diversity percentile
median_diversity_pctile <- median(met$nFeature_RNA) / nrow(normed)


##############################################################################
## Run AUCell by chunks of cells
##############################################################################

cells <- met[["cell_ID"]]
cellchunks <- data.table(cells)[,chunk:=floor((1:.N)/20000) + 1][]
for(ii in 1:cellchunks[,max(chunk)]){

  message(ii)
  cellsscore <- cellchunks[chunk==ii][["cells"]]
  chunk_counts <- normed[,cellsscore]
  set.seed(250404)
  cells_rankings <- AUCell::AUCell_buildRankings(exprMat=as(chunk_counts, "dgCMatrix"), 
                                                 ,plotStats = FALSE
                                                 ,splitByBlocks = TRUE
                                                 ,BPPARAM = BiocParallel::MulticoreParam(workers = 3)
                                                 
  )
  
  saveRDS(cells_rankings, paste0(pathway_dir, "/Data/cells_ranking_cellchunk_", ii, ".rds"))
  
  pb <- txtProgressBar(min = 0, max = nrow(chunks), style=3) 
  for(chunky in 1:nrow(chunks)){

    message(chunky)
    strt <- chunks[chunky,strt]
    stp <- chunks[chunky,stp]
    #run aucell for all gene sets 
    reschunk <- AUCell::AUCell_calcAUC(geneSets=gene.sets[strt:stp], cells_rankings, 
                                       aucMaxRank=ceiling(nrow(cells_rankings)*median_diversity_pctile), verbose = TRUE,
                                       nCores = 4,
                                      
    )
    reschunk <- as(reschunk@assays@data$AUC, "sparseMatrix")
    setTxtProgressBar(pb, chunky)
    saveRDS(reschunk, file=paste0(pathway_dir, "/Data/cellsAUC_"
                                  ,".cellschunk__",ii
                                  ,".chunk__",chunky
                                  ,".rds")
            )
    
    rm(reschunk); gc()
  } 
  gc()
    
}

# Join all cells and pathways to one matrix
cells_auc_full <- NULL
for(ii in 1:cellchunks[,max(chunk)]){
  
  cells_auc_mtx <- readRDS(file=paste0(pathway_dir, "/Data/cellsAUC_"
                                       ,".cellschunk__",ii
                                       ,".chunk__","1"
                                       ,".rds"))
  
  for(chunky in 2:nrow(chunks)){
    
    temp_mtx <- readRDS(file=paste0(pathway_dir, "/Data/cellsAUC_"
                                    ,".cellschunk__",ii
                                    ,".chunk__",chunky
                                    ,".rds"))
    cells_auc_mtx <- rbind(cells_auc_mtx, temp_mtx)
  }
  
  if(is.null(cells_auc_full)){
    cells_auc_full <- cells_auc_mtx
  } else{
    cells_auc_full <- cbind(cells_auc_full, cells_auc_mtx)
  }
}

saveRDS(cells_auc_full, file = paste0(pathway_dir, "/Data/cellsAUC_"
                                      ,"full"
                                      ,".rds"))

As this package is written in python, we start by generating an adata object from our filtered Seurat object.

Hierarchy of the domains assigned by novae:
Plot these novae clusters in XY and UMAP space. For this plotting, we switch back into R.

4.1 Identify tumor lobes
In this section we look to identify the major transcriptional differences between tumor cells in the lower dense lobe and tumor cells in the upper interdigitated lobe of the tumor.
We first manually define the two main regions of the tumor - the bottom dense, localized lobe as well as the upper interdigitated lobe.
Manually draw a polygon around the lower localized tumor lobe.
Show the code
# if there's no seurat object, read it in
if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$seurat_file_postCellTyping)
}

if(is.null(results_list$lower_lobe_cells)){
  
  ## Select outermost ring of cells to consider
  
  # Define a polygon selection function
  euclidean <- function(a, b) {
    sqrt(sum((a - b)^2))
  }
  
  select_polygon <- function(distmin = 0.01, max_points = 40){
    message("Please select points to define a polygon.  Click to the first point to stop.  First point marker is largest.")
    lims <- par("usr")
    margins <- par("plt")
    calcX <- function(x, limitss = lims, mars = margins) limitss[1] + ((x-mars[1])/(1-(1-mars[2])-mars[1]))*(limitss[2]-limitss[1])
    calcY <- function(y, limitss = lims, mars = margins) limitss[3] + ((y-mars[3])/(1-(1-mars[4])-mars[3]))*(limitss[4]-limitss[3])
    calcXY <- function(z) c(calcX(z[1]), calcY(z[2]))
    
    # determine diagonal distance in the plotting coordinate frame
    diagonalDist <- euclidean(lims[c(1,3)], lims[c(2,4)])
    
    # select first and second point and third point
    pg <- matrix(c(0,0), nrow = 1)
    pg[1, ] <- calcXY(unlist(grid::grid.locator(unit = "npc")))
    points(pg[1,1], pg[1,2], cex = 1, pch = 9, col = "magenta")
    pg <- rbind(pg, calcXY(unlist(grid::grid.locator(unit = "npc"))))
    points(pg[nrow(pg),1], pg[nrow(pg),2], cex = 0.5, pch = 9, col = "magenta")
    pg <- rbind(pg, calcXY(unlist(grid::grid.locator(unit = "npc"))))
    points(pg[nrow(pg),1], pg[nrow(pg),2], cex = 0.5, pch = 9, col = "magenta")
    
    #select additional points until a point is within the desired distance of the original point (or hit max_points limit)
    while(euclidean(pg[nrow(pg),], pg[1,]) > distmin*diagonalDist){
      pg <- rbind(pg, calcXY(unlist(grid::grid.locator(unit = "npc"))))
      points(pg[nrow(pg),1], pg[nrow(pg),2], cex = 0.5, pch = 9, col = "magenta")
      if(nrow(pg) > max_points) {
        message("You reached the max allowed points.")
        break
      }
    }
    if(nrow(pg) > 3) pg <- pg[1:(nrow(pg)-1),]
    polygon(pg[,1],pg[,2],col="#00000007",border="red")
    return(pg)
  }
  
  # Plot cells in bottom of tumor
  plot(seu.obj@meta.data$x_slide_mm, 
       seu.obj@meta.data$y_slide_mm, 
       cex = 0.01, ylim = c(-0.5,6), 
       asp=1, col = rgb(0,0,0,0.1))
  
  
  # Select outer tumor edge polygon manually
  pg_outer <- select_polygon()
  
  # which points are within the polygon
  idx_selected <- mgcv::in.out(pg_outer, as.matrix(seu.obj@meta.data[,c("x_slide_mm","y_slide_mm")] ))
  outer_cells <- seu.obj@meta.data$cell_id[idx_selected]
  
  # Add to results list
  results_list$lower_lobe_cells <- outer_cells
  saveRDS(results_list, results_list_file)
}

4.3 Contrast tumor lobes - differential expression
We use differential expression to contrast tumor cells in the two lobes, using only genes that are more likely to be expressed in tumor cells than surrounding cells (ie are unlikely to be present simply due to tumor cells overlapping with non-tumor cells at their borders).


Show the code
if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){

}

# Isolate meta for plotting

# Add lobe assignments
meta$lobe <- "none"
meta[results_list$upper_lobe_cells, "lobe"] <- "Upper"
meta[results_list$lower_lobe_cells, "lobe"] <- "Lower"

## Run DE between tumor lobes on tumor cells only

# Pre-de find neighbors
pre_de_obj <- pre_de(
  metadata = meta,
  cell_type_metadata_colname = "major_cell_type",
  mm_radius = 0.05,
  sdimx_colname = "x_slide_mm",
  sdimy_colname = "y_slide_mm",
  verbose = TRUE,
  adjacencies_only = TRUE
)

# Add total counts to metadata as DE expects
meta$totalcounts = meta$nCount_RNA

# Use overlap metric to identify genes to test
overlap_metrics <- 
smiDE::overlap_ratio_metric(assay_matrix = seu.obj@assays$RNA$data,
                           metadata = meta,
                           cluster_col = "major_cell_type",
                           radius = 0.05,
                           #split_neighbors_by_colname = "Run_Tissue_name",
                           sdimx_col = "x_slide_mm",
                           sdimy_col = "y_slide_mm"
                           )

# Save overlap metrics
saveRDS(overlap_metrics, file = paste0(tumorDE_dir, "/Data/overlap_metrics.rds"))

# Only analyze genes with ratio less than or equal to 1
analysis_genes <- overlap_metrics[major_cell_type=="Tumor" & ratio <= 1]$target

# DE test dependence on tumor lobe
de_obj <- smi_de(
  assay_matrix = seu.obj@assays$RNA@counts[analysis_genes,],
  metadata = meta[which(meta[,"major_cell_type"] == "Tumor"),],
  formula = ~RankNorm(otherct_expr) + lobe + offset(log(totalcounts)),
  pre_de_obj = pre_de_obj,
  groupVar = "lobe",
  neighbor_expr_cell_type_metadata_colname = "major_cell_type",
  neighbor_expr_totalcount_normalize = TRUE,
  neighbor_expr_totalcount_scalefactor = NULL,
  family = "nbinom2",
  targets = analysis_genes,
  nCores = 20
)

# Save objects
saveRDS(pre_de_obj, file = paste0(tumorDE_dir, "/Data/pre_de_obj.rds"))
saveRDS(de_obj, file = paste0(tumorDE_dir, "/Data/de_obj_tumorGenes.rds"))

5.2 Immune-related pathways
We generate spatial plots of a number of immune-related pathways, focusing only on expression within tumor cells. We perform spatial smoothing across tumor cells.


Show the code
# if there's no seurat object, read it in
if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$seurat_file_postCellTyping)
}

meta <- seu.obj@meta.data

# Read in AUCell results
cells_auc_full <- readRDS(paste0(pathway_dir, "/Data/cellsAUC_"
                                      ,"full"
                                      ,".rds"))

# Calculate smoothed neighborhood expression
xy <- seu.obj@meta.data[,c("x_slide_mm", "y_slide_mm")]
xy$cell_ID <- rownames(xy)

# Use a smoothing function modified from https://nanostring-biostats.github.io/CosMx-Analysis-Scratch-Space/posts/marker-gene-smoothing/
xy_nn <- function(xy, n_neighbors=50){
  xy <- as.data.table(xy)
 
    ## identify nearest n_neighbors (+1 includes the cell as a neighbor to itself)
  nn_xy <- RANN::nn2(xy[,.(x_slide_mm, y_slide_mm)],k = n_neighbors + 1)$nn.idx
  nn_xy <- data.table::melt(cbind(xy[,.(cell_ID)], data.table(nn_xy))
                              , id.vars=c("cell_ID", "V1"))
  colnames(nn_xy) <- c("cell_ID1", "cell_ID1_idx", "neighbor", "cell_ID2_idx")
  nn_xy <- merge(nn_xy
                   , nn_xy[,.(cell_ID2=cell_ID1, cell_ID2_idx=cell_ID1_idx)][
                     ,unique(.SD)],by="cell_ID2_idx")
  
  ## Cell x cell neighbor indicator matrix
  wxy <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(i = c(unique(nn_xy$cell_ID1_idx), nn_xy$cell_ID2_idx)
                                ,j=c(unique(nn_xy$cell_ID1_idx), nn_xy$cell_ID1_idx)
                                ,x=1)
  
  rownames(wxy) <- colnames(wxy) <- nn_xy[order(nn_xy$cell_ID1_idx),unique(cell_ID1)]
  
  ## Column standardize, so that columns (cells) sum to 1, and each neighbor given equal weight.
  mxy <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(i=1:ncol(wxy)
                                ,j=1:ncol(wxy)
                                ,x=1/Matrix::colSums(wxy)
                                )
  dimnames(mxy) <- dimnames(wxy)
  smoother <- mxy %*% wxy
  smoother <- smoother[,xy$cell_ID]
  return(smoother)
}

Show the code
# Read in DE object
de_obj <- readRDS(paste0(immNeigh_dir, "/Data/cd8teff_broadNiche_de_obj.rds"))

# Extract estimated means
em_res <- results(de_obj)$emmeans %>% filter(term == "broad_niche")

# Extract pairwise results
pairwise.df <- results(de_obj, "pairwise")$pairwise

# Conversions of some data names
if("broad_niche_v2" %in% pairwise.df$term){
  pairwise.df$term = gsub("broad_niche_v2", "broad_niche", pairwise.df$term)
}
pairwise.df <- pairwise.df %>% filter(term == "broad_niche")

# Add fdr
pairwise.df$fdr = p.adjust(pairwise.df$p.value, method = "fdr")

# Save pairwise results to a table to be included as supplementary information.
write.csv(as.data.frame(pairwise.df)[,c(setdiff(colnames(pairwise.df), c("df", "null", "fold_change")))],
          file = paste0(immNeigh_dir, "/Data/CD8TcytotoxicBroadNicheDE_table.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)


# Select all genes that have fdr < 0.05 in any comparison
de_genes <- pairwise.df %>% filter(fdr < 0.05) %>% pull(target) %>% unique()

# Extract estimated means for all de genes
em_de <- em_res %>% filter(target %in% de_genes)

# Filter for significant genes (FDR < 0.05) and count number and type of DE comparisons per gene
de_signature <- pairwise.df %>%
  filter(fdr < 0.05) %>%
  distinct(target, contrast) %>%
  group_by(target) %>%
  summarise(
    de_signature = paste(sort(unique(contrast)), collapse = "_"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Prepare expression matrix
expr_matrix <- em_de %>%
  dplyr::select(target, level, response) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = level, values_from = response) %>%
  column_to_rownames("target")

# Scale each row to [0, 1] by dividing by row max
expr_scaled <- t(apply(expr_matrix, 1, function(x) x / max(x, na.rm = TRUE)))

# Create annotation for DE count
# Merge DE count with expression matrix rownames
de_annotation <- data.frame(target = rownames(expr_scaled)) %>%
  left_join(de_signature, by = "target") 

# Define color palette for DE signature

de_levels <- c(
  "none",  # no DE
  "exterior stroma / interior stroma",
  "exterior stroma / tumor bed",
  "interior stroma / tumor bed",
  "exterior stroma / interior stroma_exterior stroma / tumor bed",
  "exterior stroma / interior stroma_interdigitated stroma / tumor bed",
  "exterior stroma / tumor bed_interior stroma / tumor bed",
  "exterior stroma / interior stroma_exterior stroma / tumor bed_interior stroma / tumor bed"
)

de_annotation$de_signature <- factor(de_annotation$de_signature,
                                     levels = de_levels)

# Assign colors based on number of comparisons
de_colors <- c(
  "none" = "#d9d9d9",  # neutral gray
  "exterior stroma / interior stroma" = "#91bfdb",  # cool blue
  "exterior stroma / tumor bed" = "#a6d96a",  # cool green
  "interior stroma / tumor bed" = "#c2a5cf",  # cool purple
  "exterior stroma / interior stroma_exterior stroma / tumor bed" = "#ffd92f",  # bright yellow
  "exterior stroma / interior stroma_interior stroma / tumor bed" = "#f46d43",  # warm coral
  "exterior stroma / tumor bed_interior stroma / tumor bed" = "#e6a141",  # warm amber
  "exterior stroma / interior stroma_exterior stroma / tumor bed_interior stroma / tumor bed" = "#d73027"  # hot red
)

## Cluster genes within each group

# Create a list to store ordered gene names
ordered_genes <- c()

# Loop through each DE signature group
for (group in de_levels) {
  genes_in_group <- de_annotation %>%
    filter(de_signature == group) %>%
    pull(target)
  
  if (length(genes_in_group) > 1) {
    # Subset expression matrix
    submatrix <- expr_scaled[genes_in_group, ]
    
    # Compute hierarchical clustering
    hc <- hclust(dist(submatrix))
    
    # Get ordered gene names
    ordered_genes <- c(ordered_genes, genes_in_group[hc$order])
  } else {
    # If only one gene, just add it
    ordered_genes <- c(ordered_genes, genes_in_group)
  }
}

# Set gene order for expression matrix and annotation
expr_scaled_ordered <- expr_scaled[ordered_genes, ]

# Reorder annotation to match
de_annotation_ordered <- de_annotation[match(ordered_genes, de_annotation$target), ]

# Use shorter DE signature names
# Mapping long DE signature strings to short labels
de_signature_labels <- c(
  "none" = "None",
  "exterior stroma / interior stroma" = "E vs I",
  "exterior stroma / tumor bed" = "E vs T",
  "interior stroma / tumor bed" = "I vs T",
  "exterior stroma / interior stroma_exterior stroma / tumor bed" = "E vs I & E vs T",
  "exterior stroma / interior stroma_interior stroma / tumor bed" = "E vs I & I vs T",
  "exterior stroma / tumor bed_interior stroma / tumor bed" = "E vs T & I vs T",
  "exterior stroma / interior stroma_exterior stroma / tumor bed_interior stroma / tumor bed" = "All (E vs I, E vs T, I vs T)"
)

names(de_colors) <- de_signature_labels[names(de_colors)]

# Apply to factor levels
de_annotation_ordered$de_signature <- factor(
  de_annotation_ordered$de_signature,
  levels = names(de_signature_labels),
  labels = de_signature_labels
)

# Create row annotation
row_ha <- rowAnnotation(
  DE_Signature = de_annotation_ordered$de_signature,
  col = list(DE_Signature = de_colors),
  show_annotation_name = FALSE,
  annotation_legend_param = list(
    DE_Signature = list(title = "Significant contrasts")
  )

)

## Label specific genes of interest


# Identify two representative genes per group
# Add gene names to expression matrix
expr_scaled_ordered_df <- as.data.frame(expr_scaled_ordered)
expr_scaled_ordered_df$target <- rownames(expr_scaled_ordered_df)

# Target list chosen based on expected biology, unexpected but plausible, and present in one or more contrasts
genes_of_interest <- c("PDCD1", "KLRG1", "CXCR4", "RPL28", 
                       "SARDH", "CD69",
                        "KLRB1", "GIMAP4",  "CD44",
                       "PRDM1", "KLRK1", "CCR2", "EVL", "GNLY", "H2BC4", "H1-4", 
                       "ID2", "CXCR3", "ANXA1")


# Find the indices of these genes in the matrix
gene_indices = which(rownames(expr_scaled_ordered) %in% genes_of_interest)

# Create a row annotation with anno_mark()
# This annotation will place the gene labels on the right side.
gene_labels_anno = rowAnnotation(
  gene_labels = anno_mark(
    at = gene_indices,
    labels = rownames(expr_scaled_ordered)[gene_indices],
    labels_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10),  # Adjust label font size
    link_width = unit(5, "mm")       # Adjust line length
  )
)

# Rename columns to include shorthand
colnames(expr_scaled_ordered) <- dplyr::recode(
  colnames(expr_scaled_ordered),
  "exterior stroma" = "Exterior stroma (E)",
  "interior stroma" = "Interior stroma (I)",
  "tumor bed" = "Tumor bed (T)"
)

# Generate heatmap
hm <- Heatmap(
  expr_scaled_ordered,
  name = "Scaled Expression",
  col = colorRamp2(c(0, 1), c("white", "grey30")),
  cluster_rows = FALSE,
  cluster_columns = TRUE,
  show_row_names = FALSE,
  left_annotation = row_ha,
  row_split = de_annotation_ordered$de_signature,
  row_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 0),
  show_row_dend = FALSE,
  show_column_dend = FALSE,
  right_annotation = gene_labels_anno
)

png(filename = paste0(immNeigh_dir, "/Plots/heatmap_cd8teff_broadNiche_v2_selectedGenes.png"),

                                  ,cluster_col = "minor_cell_type"
                                  ,sdimx_col = "x_slide_mm"

   smi_de(assay_matrix = seu.obj[["RNA"]]@counts[genes_to_analyze,]
          ,metadata = seu.obj@meta.data[which(seu.obj@meta.data$minor_cell_type == ct),]

          ,neighbor_expr_totalcount_normalize = TRUE

7.1 Smoothed glycolysis pathway scores
In this section we focus on glycolysis and the impact of the surrounding glycolytic environment on gene expression.
We start by looking at glycolysis in space. We use pathway calculations from AUCell to generate glycolysis pathway scores for every cellular neighborhood.
Show the code
# if there's no seurat object, read it in

# Read in AUCell results

# Extract glycolysis pathway scores
glyc <- cells_auc_full["REACTOME_GLYCOLYSIS",]
meta <- seu.obj@meta.data
meta$glyc <- glyc[meta$cell_ID]

# total expression by cell type:
sumglyc <- by(meta$glyc, meta$major_cell_type, sum)
sumglyc["Tumor"] / sum(sumglyc)

# Calculate smoothed neighborhood expression
xy <- seu.obj@meta.data[,c("x_slide_mm", "y_slide_mm")]
xy$cell_ID <- rownames(xy)

# Use a smoothing function modified from https://nanostring-biostats.github.io/CosMx-Analysis-Scratch-Space/posts/marker-gene-smoothing/
xy_nn <- function(xy, n_neighbors=50){
  xy <- as.data.table(xy)
 
    ## identify nearest n_neighbors (+1 includes the cell as a neighbor to itself)
  nn_xy <- RANN::nn2(xy[,.(x_slide_mm, y_slide_mm)],k = n_neighbors + 1)$nn.idx
  nn_xy <- data.table::melt(cbind(xy[,.(cell_ID)], data.table(nn_xy))
                              , id.vars=c("cell_ID", "V1"))
  colnames(nn_xy) <- c("cell_ID1", "cell_ID1_idx", "neighbor", "cell_ID2_idx")
  nn_xy <- merge(nn_xy
                   , nn_xy[,.(cell_ID2=cell_ID1, cell_ID2_idx=cell_ID1_idx)][
                     ,unique(.SD)],by="cell_ID2_idx")
  
  ## Cell x cell neighbor indicator matrix
  wxy <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(i = c(unique(nn_xy$cell_ID1_idx), nn_xy$cell_ID2_idx)
                                ,j=c(unique(nn_xy$cell_ID1_idx), nn_xy$cell_ID1_idx)
                                ,x=1)
  
  rownames(wxy) <- colnames(wxy) <- nn_xy[order(nn_xy$cell_ID1_idx),unique(cell_ID1)]
  
  ## Column standardize, so that columns (cells) sum to 1, and each neighbor given equal weight.
  mxy <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(i=1:ncol(wxy)
                                ,j=1:ncol(wxy)
                                ,x=1/Matrix::colSums(wxy)
                                )
  dimnames(mxy) <- dimnames(wxy)
  smoother <- mxy %*% wxy
  smoother <- smoother[,xy$cell_ID]
  return(smoother)
}

# Smoothed glycolysis pathway

7.2 Differential expression as a function of neighborhood glycolysis
Here we run DE on every cell type to try to understand how every cell type changes as a function of glycolysis levels in the neighborhood it finds itself in. The prediction is that we might find some genes that are consistently up or down regulated across all or many cell types. This might also point us towards cell types that are more or less responsive / susceptible to the surrounding glycolysis environment. As additional factors in our model, we also include niche and the number of each tumor cell type in the 50 nearest neighbors. For speed in making this many comparisons, we work with normalized counts and a gaussian model.


Show the code
if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$seurat_file_postCellTyping)
}

## Isolate meta data and add neighborhood glycolysis activity
meta <- seu.obj@meta.data

smoothed_glyc <- readRDS(file = paste0(metabolism_dir, "/Data/xy_smoothed_glycolysis.rds"))

meta$smoothed_glyc <- smoothed_glyc[1,meta$cell_id]

# Add number of each type of tumor cell in 50 nearest neighbors
coords <- as.matrix(meta[, c("x_slide_mm", "y_slide_mm")])
K <- 50
idx <- FNN::get.knn(coords, k = K)$nn.index  # (N x K), self is not included here

# Count cells in neighborhood
types   <- as.character(meta$minor_cell_type)
targets <- c("LUM+ tumor","HPD+ tumor","PGC+ tumor","KRT16+ tumor","Proliferating tumor")

neighbor_counts <- lapply(targets, function(lbl) {
  is_target <- (types == lbl)
  mat <- matrix(is_target[idx], nrow = nrow(idx), ncol = ncol(idx))
  rowSums(mat)
})
names(neighbor_counts) <- targets

meta$neighboring_lum  <- neighbor_counts[["LUM+ tumor"]]
meta$neighboring_hpd  <- neighbor_counts[["HPD+ tumor"]]
meta$neighboring_pgc  <- neighbor_counts[["PGC+ tumor"]]
meta$neighboring_krt  <- neighbor_counts[["KRT16+ tumor"]]
meta$neighboring_prol <- neighbor_counts[["Proliferating tumor"]]

# Add novae domain
novae_9 <- readRDS(paste0(niche_dir, "/Data/novae_domains_9_assignments.rds"))
meta$novae <- novae_9[rownames(meta)]

## Prep pre-de files that are conserved across cell types

# Pre-de find neighbors
pre_de_obj <- pre_de(
  metadata = meta,
  cell_type_metadata_colname = "minor_cell_type",
  mm_radius = 0.05,
  sdimx_colname = "x_slide_mm",
  sdimy_colname = "y_slide_mm",
  verbose = TRUE
)

# Save pre-de results
saveRDS(pre_de_obj, file = paste0(metabolism_dir, "/Data/pre_de_obj.rds"))

# Run overlap filter

overlap_metrics <- 
overlap_ratio_metric(assay_matrix = seu.obj@assays$RNA$data,
                           metadata = meta,
                           cluster_col = "minor_cell_type",
                           radius = 0.05,
                           sdimx_col = "x_slide_mm",
                           sdimy_col = "y_slide_mm"
                           )

# Save overlap metrics
saveRDS(overlap_metrics, file = paste0(metabolism_dir, "/Data/overlap_metrics.rds"))

# Add total counts to metadata as DE expects
meta$totalcounts = meta$nCount_RNA

# Work with total count normalized data
counts <- seu.obj@assays$RNA$counts
scaling_factor <- mean(seu.obj@meta.data$nCount_RNA)
norm <- counts %*% 
  Matrix::Diagonal(x = scaling_factor/seu.obj@meta.data$nCount_RNA,
                         names=colnames(counts)) 
 

# Iterate through each cell type

for(ct in unique(meta$minor_cell_type)){
  print(paste0("Starting cell type ", ct, " at ", Sys.time()))
  
  # Only analyze genes with overlap ratio less than or equal to 1
  analysis_genes <- overlap_metrics[minor_cell_type == ct & ratio <= 1]$target
  
  # Extract counts for analysis genes only
  sub_counts <- norm[analysis_genes,]
  
  # DE test dependence on neighborhood glycolysis
  de_obj <- smiDE::smi_de(
    assay_matrix = sub_counts,
    metadata = meta[which(meta[,"minor_cell_type"]== ct),],
    formula = ~RankNorm(otherct_expr) + smoothed_glyc + novae + neighboring_lum + neighboring_hpd + neighboring_pgc + neighboring_krt + neighboring_prol,
    pre_de_obj = pre_de_obj,
    groupVar = "smoothed_glyc",
    neighbor_expr_cell_type_metadata_colname = "minor_cell_type",
    neighbor_expr_totalcount_normalize = FALSE,
    neighbor_expr_totalcount_scalefactor = NULL,
    family = "gaussian",
    targets = analysis_genes,
    nCores = 24
  )
  
  # Save objects
  saveRDS(de_obj, file = paste0(metabolism_dir, "/Data/ct_", gsub("\\+", "", gsub(" ", "_", ct)), "_smoothedGlycolysis_de_obj_plusNicheNeighborTumor.rds"))
}


For every cell type, we make a volcano plot showing the estimated difference in expression between high and low glycolysis neighborhoods for each tested gene. Genes whose difference reached significance are colored and a subset are labeled. Also generate a table of DE results to be included as a supplementary table. Print each cell type to a separate sheet.


Show the code
# Generate a list of pairwise DE results files
de_result_files <- dir(paste0(metabolism_dir, "/Data/"), pattern = "^ct_.*smoothedGlycolysis_de_obj_plusNicheNeighborTumor\\.rds$")

# Make a list of results to print to table
res_list <- list()

#de_res_list <- list()
for(de_file in de_result_files){
  de_obj <- readRDS(paste0(metabolism_dir, "/Data/", de_file))
  
  # Extract cell type
  ct <- gsub("ct_", "", gsub("_smoothedGlycolysis_de_obj_plusNicheNeighborTumor.rds", "", de_file))
  
  # Extract pairwise results, which correspond to difference between mean and 1SD of glycolysis score
  pairwise.df <- results(de_obj, "pairwise")$pairwise
  pairwise.df <- pairwise.df %>% filter(term == "smoothed_glyc") 
  
  # Adjust p-value
  pairwise.df$p.adj <- p.adjust(pairwise.df$p.value, method = "fdr") # Use fdr for padj
  res_list[[ct]] <- as.data.frame(pairwise.df)[,c("target", "estimate", "SE", "df", "t.ratio", "p.value",
                                                  "fold_change", "modelest_cpc_1", "modelest_cpc_2",
                                                  "term", "p.adj")]
  
  # Plot for each contrast, largely adapting smiDE volcano plot code
  for(contrast in unique(pairwise.df$contrast)){
    pairwise.df_i <- as.data.frame(pairwise.df)[which(pairwise.df$contrast == contrast),]

    # Extract comparison
    cc = pairwise.df_i$contrast[1]
    compv = compv <- strsplit(as.character(cc), "\\ vs.\\ ")[[1]]
    if(grepl(" [\\/-]\\ ", cc)) compv <- strsplit(as.character(cc), "\\ [\\/-]\\ ")[[1]]

    ## Plot with scaled estimates to adjust for expression levels

    # Large estimates disrupt scaling, so cap them and change the shape
    pairwise.df_i$scaled_estimate <- pairwise.df_i$estimate / pairwise.df_i$modelest_cpc_2
    pairwise.df_i$scaled_estimate_capped <- pmax(pmin(pairwise.df_i$scaled_estimate, 0.95), -0.95)
    pairwise.df_i$capped <- abs(pairwise.df_i$scaled_estimate) > 0.95

    # x labels
    xrng <- c((max(abs(pairwise.df_i$scaled_estimate_capped)) * -1),
              max(abs(pairwise.df_i$scaled_estimate_capped)))
    xrng <- pretty(xrng)

    # Set up y labels
    nDigits <- function(x) suppressWarnings(as.integer(strsplit(x = formatC(formatC(x = x, format="e"), format = "s"), split = "e")[[1]][2]))
    pairwise.df_i <- as.data.table(pairwise.df_i)
    bonf<- pairwise.df_i[,0.05/(uniqueN(target) * uniqueN(contrast))]
    max.y <- nDigits(min(pairwise.df_i[,min(p.value)+10^-300], signif(bonf / 2, 1)))

    ybrk <- 1 * 10^pretty( c(-1:(max.y)) )
    ylab <- ybrk

    # Add coloring
    est_cutoff = 0.1
    pairwise.df_i$sig_group = paste0("P adj > 0.05\nand/or\nScaled exp diff < ", est_cutoff)
    pairwise.df_i$sig_group[intersect(which(pairwise.df_i$p.adj < 0.05),
                                      which((pairwise.df_i$scaled_estimate) > est_cutoff))] <- compv[1]
    pairwise.df_i$sig_group[intersect(which(pairwise.df_i$p.adj < 0.05),
                                      which((pairwise.df_i$scaled_estimate) < -est_cutoff))] <- compv[2]
    my_cols = c("tomato3", "lightskyblue3", "lightgrey")
    names(my_cols) = c(compv[1],
                       compv[2],
                       paste0("P adj > 0.05\nand/or\nScaled exp diff < ", est_cutoff))

    # Set up yintercept for pval cutoff
    pval_cutoff_y <- pairwise.df %>% filter(p.adj < 0.05) %>% pull(p.value) %>% max()

    # Plot with top DE genes labeled
    ggplot(pairwise.df_i,
           aes(x = scaled_estimate_capped, y = p.value + 10^-300)) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = pval_cutoff_y, linetype = 2) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = est_cutoff, linetype = 2) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = -est_cutoff, linetype = 2) +
      geom_point(aes(color = sig_group, shape = capped)) +
      scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 19, `TRUE` = 17)) +
      scale_color_manual(values = my_cols, name = "Significance group") +
      scale_y_continuous(trans = smiDE:::change_axis_revlog_trans(base=10),
                         breaks = ybrk,
                         labels = formatC(ylab, format = "e", digits = 0)) +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = xrng, limits = range(xrng)) +
      theme_bw() +
      ylab("p value") +
      xlab(paste0("Lower neighborhood glycolysis ", sprintf('\u2190'),
                  " Scaled estimated expression difference ",
                  sprintf('\u2192'), "Higher neighborhood glycolysis" )) +
      geom_text(data = pairwise.df[1,],
                aes(label = paste0(sum(pairwise.df_i$sig_group == compv[1]), "\ngenes"),
                    x = max(xrng)*0.8, y = sqrt(min(ybrk))),
                color = my_cols[[compv[1]]]) +
      geom_text(data = pairwise.df[1,],
                aes(label = paste0(sum(pairwise.df_i$sig_group == compv[2]), "\ngenes"),
                    x = min(xrng)*0.8, y = sqrt(min(ybrk))),
                color = my_cols[[compv[2]]]) +
      ggtitle(paste0(ct,
                     " gene expression as a function of glycolysis in the neighborhood")) +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 8)) +
      theme(axis.title.x = element_text(size = 6)) +
      theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size = 6)) +
      geom_label_repel(data = pairwise.df_i %>% filter(!grepl("P adj", sig_group)),
                       aes(x = scaled_estimate_capped, y = p.value + 10^-300,
                           label = target)) +
      guides(shape = "none")
    ggsave(filename = paste0(metabolism_dir, "/Plots/", gsub("+", "", ct), "_volcano_GLYCneighborhoodDifferences_scaledEstDiff_", compv[1], "vs",
                             compv[2], "_withGeneLabels_v2.png"))
  }
}

Additionally, we make summary plots to show results across all cell types. We generate a bar plot showing the number of genes called as significantly different across cell types and a heatmap showing most consistent genes across cell types.


Show the code
# Generate a list of pairwise DE results
de_result_files <- dir(paste0(metabolism_dir, "/Data/"), pattern = "^ct_.*smoothedGlycolysis_de_obj_plusNicheNeighborTumor\\.rds$")

de_res_list <- list()
for(de_file in de_result_files){
  res <- readRDS(paste0(metabolism_dir, "/Data/", de_file))
  
  pairwise.df <- results(res)$pairwise
  pairwise.df <- pairwise.df %>% filter(term == "smoothed_glyc")
  
  # Extract cell type
  ct <- gsub("ct_", "", gsub("_smoothedGlycolysis_de_obj_plusNicheNeighborTumor.rds", "", de_file))
  
  # Convert underscore to space
  ct <- gsub("_", " ", ct)
  
  # Add a + for tumor cells except proliferating
  ct <- gsub(" tumor", "+ tumor", ct)
  ct <- gsub("Proliferating\\+", "Proliferating", ct)
  
  de_res_list[[ct]] <- pairwise.df
}

# Define a function to add the adjusted p-values
add_p_adj <- function(df) {
  df$p.adj <- p.adjust(df$p.value, method = "fdr") # Note the method used here
  return(df)
}

# Apply the function to each data frame in the list
de_res_list <- lapply(de_res_list, add_p_adj)


## Barplot showing the number of genes that are up or down regulated per cell type
# count significant genes
sig_genes <- list()

# Iterate through each data frame in the list
for (ct_name in names(de_res_list)) {
  df <- de_res_list[[ct_name]]
  
  # Filter for significant genes
  significant_genes <- df %>% filter(p.adj < 0.05) %>% filter(abs(estimate/modelest_cpc_2) > 0.1)
  
  # Count upregulated genes
  upregulated <- sum(significant_genes$estimate/significant_genes$modelest_cpc_2 > 0.1)
  
  # Count downregulated genes
  downregulated <- sum(significant_genes$estimate/significant_genes$modelest_cpc_2 < -0.1)
  
  # Count total genes evaluated
  tot_genes <- nrow(df)
  
  # Store the results in a data frame
  sig_genes[[ct_name]] <- data.frame(
    ct = ct_name,
    direction = c("up", "down"),
    nGenes = c(upregulated, downregulated),
    totGenes = tot_genes
  )
}

# Combine all results into a single data frame
sig_genes <- do.call(rbind, sig_genes)

# Order cell types by total genes changes
tot_genes_changed <- aggregate(sig_genes$nGenes ~ sig_genes$ct, FUN = "sum")
ct_order <- tot_genes_changed[order(tot_genes_changed[,2], decreasing = T),1]
sig_genes$ct <- factor(sig_genes$ct, levels = ct_order)

# Order direction for legend plotting
sig_genes$direction <- factor(sig_genes$direction, levels = c("up", "down"))

ggplot(sig_genes, aes(x = ct, y = ifelse(direction == "up", nGenes, -nGenes), fill = direction)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("up" = "tomato3", "down" = "lightskyblue3")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Upregulated and downregulated genes per cell type\nin neighborhoods of high glycolysis",
       #x = "Cell Type",
       y = "Number of Genes",
       fill = "Direction of change") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 12),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        legend.position = c(0.9, 0.9))
ggsave(paste0(metabolism_dir, "/Plots/Barplot_sigGenes_glycolysisNeighborhood_byCT_scaledEstDiff_v2.png"),
       width = 10, height = 4, units = "in")

# Heatmap showing differences across multiple cell types
## Choose genes to show
# Initialize lists to store upregulated and downregulated genes
upregulated_genes <- list()
downregulated_genes <- list()

# Iterate through each data frame in the list
for (ct_name in names(de_res_list)) {
  df <- de_res_list[[ct_name]]
  
  # Filter for significant upregulated genes
  significant_upregulated <- df %>% filter(p.adj < 0.05) %>% filter(estimate/modelest_cpc_2 > 0.1)
  upregulated_genes[[ct_name]] <- significant_upregulated$target
  
  # Filter for significant downregulated genes
  significant_downregulated <- df %>% filter(p.adj < 0.05) %>% filter(estimate/modelest_cpc_2 < -0.1)
  downregulated_genes[[ct_name]] <- significant_downregulated$target
}

# Combine all upregulated and downregulated genes into single vectors
all_upregulated_genes <- unlist(upregulated_genes)
all_downregulated_genes <- unlist(downregulated_genes)

# Count the occurrences of each gene
up_gene_counts <- table(all_upregulated_genes)
down_gene_counts <- table(all_downregulated_genes)

# Sort genes by their counts in descending order
sorted_up_genes <- sort(up_gene_counts, decreasing = TRUE)
sorted_down_genes <- sort(down_gene_counts, decreasing = TRUE)

# Select genes that are significant in at least 4 cell types in a consistent direction
top_up_genes <- names(sorted_up_genes)[which(sorted_up_genes > 3)]
top_down_genes <- names(sorted_down_genes)[which(sorted_down_genes > 3)]

# Combine the top genes
top_genes <- unique(c(top_up_genes, rev(top_down_genes)))

## Make df of genes to show
# Initialize an empty data frame to store the heatmap data
heatmap_data <- data.frame()

# Iterate through each data frame in the list
for (ct_name in names(de_res_list)) {
  df <- de_res_list[[ct_name]]
  
  # Filter for the top genes
  df_top_genes <- df %>% filter(target %in% top_genes)
  
  # Add cell type information
  df_top_genes$ct <- ct_name
  
  # Append to the heatmap data frame
  heatmap_data <- rbind(heatmap_data, df_top_genes)
}

# Add a column for significance
heatmap_data$significant <- heatmap_data$p.adj < 0.05

# Set order of genes to have most consistently up -> most consistently down
heatmap_data$target <- factor(heatmap_data$target, levels = top_genes)

# Set order of cell types to align with other figures and be grouped by major type
heatmap_data$ct <- factor(heatmap_data$ct,
                          levels = gsub("_", " ", names(results_list$minor_cell_type_color_pal_manual)))

## Plot it

# Create the dot plot heatmap
ggplot(heatmap_data, aes(x = ct, y = target)) +
  geom_point(size = 0) +
  geom_point(data = heatmap_data %>% filter(significant == TRUE),
             aes(x = ct, y = target), color = "black", size = 4, shape = 18) +
  geom_point(data = heatmap_data, 
             aes(x = ct, y = target, color = estimate/modelest_cpc_2, shape = significant),
             size = 3) +
  scale_color_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 0,
                        limits = c(-1, 1),
                        oob = squish,
                        breaks = c(-1, 0, 1),
                        labels = c("<-1", "0", ">1")) +
  scale_size_manual(values = c(2,3), guide = "none") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c('TRUE' = 18, 'FALSE' = 19), guide = "none") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Heatmap of Differentially Expressed Genes",
       x = "Cell Type",
       y = "Gene",
       color = "Scaled estimated difference") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
ggsave(paste0(metabolism_dir, "/Plots/heatmap_ct_x_gene_mostDE_glycolysisNeighborhood_scaledEstDiff_v2.png"),
       width = 8, height = 8, units = "in")

8.1 Assign proliferation scores
Here we characterize regions of low cancer cell profliferation.
We start by assigning proliferation scores to each cell, using Seurat’s cell cycle scoring method.
Next, we load in basic data.
Show the code
library(data.table) 
library(InSituCor)
library(scales)
library(pheatmap)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(smiDE)
library(fgsea)  
library(dplyr)
library(alphahull)
library(Seurat)
library(SeuratObject)

source("patchDE utils.R")

#### load data ------------------------------

raw <- Matrix::t(readRDS(paste0(analysis_dir, "/Robjects/raw_exp_mat.rds")))
xy <- readRDS(paste0(analysis_dir, "/Robjects/xy.rds"))
clustdf <- readRDS(paste0(analysis_dir, "/Robjects/cell_types.rds"))
clust <- clustdf$major_cell_type
iscancer <- clust == "Tumor"
cellcycle <- readRDS(paste0(prolif_dir, "/Data/cell_cycle_predictions.rds"))
cellcyclecanceronly <- replace(cellcycle, !iscancer, "notcancer")
niches <- readRDS(paste0(analysis_dir, "/niches/Data/novae_domains_9_assignments.rds"))
seu <- readRDS(paste0(analysis_dir, "/Robjects/seurat_object_postCellTyping.rds"))
annot <- seu@meta.data
stopifnot(identical(annot$cell_ID, rownames(raw)))
rm(seu)
annot$celltype <- clust

# rotated xy:
xy21 <- xy[, 2:1]
xy21[, 2] <- mean(xy21[, 2]) - xy21[, 2]
Now we’ll partition the tissue into regions of high/low tumor proliferation:
Show the code
# there are islands of G1 phase, otherwise cancer cells are mostly G2/M/S... what explains the islands where it's failing to proliferate?
if (!file.exists(paste0(prolif_dir, "/Data/neighbors100.RDS"))) {
  neighbors100 <- InSituCor:::nearestNeighborGraph(x = xy[, 1], y = xy[, 2], N = 100)
  saveRDS(neighbors100, file = paste0(prolif_dir, "/Data/neighbors100.RDS"))
} else {
  neighbors100 <- readRDS(paste0(prolif_dir, "/Data/neighbors100.RDS"))
}

if (!file.exists(paste0(prolif_dir, "/Data/neighborhoodcelltypes.RDS"))) {
  # neighbor counts of tumor cells in each cell cycle phase
  nphase <- InSituCor:::neighbor_tabulate(cellcyclecanceronly, neighbors100) 
  # neighbor counts of cell types:
  neighborhoodcelltypes <- InSituCor:::neighbor_tabulate(clust, neighbors100) 
  saveRDS(nphase, file = paste0(prolif_dir, "/Data/nphase.RDS"))
  saveRDS(neighborhoodcelltypes, file = paste0(prolif_dir, "/Data/neighborhoodcelltypes.RDS"))
} else {
  nphase <- readRDS(paste0(prolif_dir, "/Data/nphase.RDS"))
  neighborhoodcelltypes <- readRDS(paste0(prolif_dir, "/Data/neighborhoodcelltypes.RDS"))
}
rm(neighbors100)

# rate of proliferating cancer cells in neighborhood:
prop_g2ms <- rowSums(nphase[, c("G2M", "S")]) / rowSums(nphase[, c("G1", "G2M", "S")])
prop_g2ms[is.na(prop_g2ms)] <- 0
# number of cancer cells in neighborhood:
ncancer_all <- rowSums(nphase[, c("G1", "G2M", "S")])
ncancer_cycling <- rowSums(nphase[, c("G2M", "S")])
ncancer_resting <- nphase[, "G1"]


#### What characterizes cancer cells in highly proliferative regions? -------------

# classify cancer cells as occupying proliferative/quiescent regions:
use <- (clust == "Tumor") & (ncancer_all >= 20) 
hist(prop_g2ms[use], breaks = 25)
abline(v = 0.5, col = 2)
prolifcat <- c("quiescent", "proliferative")[1 + (prop_g2ms > 0.5)]

## summarize tumor proliferation context:
table(prolifcat[iscancer]) / sum(table(prolifcat[iscancer]))

# polygons around quiescent areas:
dbuse <- (prolifcat == "quiescent") & (iscancer)
db <- dbscan::dbscan(xy[dbuse, ], eps = 0.05, minPts = 20)
if (!file.exists(paste0(prolif_dir, "/Data/qpolys.RDS"))) {
  qpolys <- list()
  for (i in setdiff(unique(db$cluster), 0)) {
    if (i %% 10 == 0){print(i)}
    inds <- which(dbuse)[db$cluster == i]
    qpolys[[as.character(i)]] <- alphahull::ahull(xy21[inds, ], alpha = 0.04)

    arcs <- qpolys[[as.character(i)]]$arcs
    arcs_clean <- arcs[(arcs[, "r"] > 0) & (arcs[, "end1"] != arcs[, "end2"]), ]
    qpolys[[as.character(i)]]$arcs <- arcs_clean
  }
  saveRDS(qpolys, file = paste0(prolif_dir, "/Data/qpolys.RDS"))
} else {
  qpolys <- readRDS(paste0(prolif_dir, "/Data/qpolys.RDS"))
}

# show the cell type results and the classification:
